what_it_does: Diffusion models (AI systems that generate images by gradually denoising) work in many timesteps, each requiring the GPU to load lots of data from memory and do math. This creates a memory traffic jam. MHDiff solves this by noticing that some pixels are more important than others. The key insight: use high precision (very accurate numbers) only for those important pixels, and use low precision (simpler rounded numbers) for everything else. The system then packs these different precision values into a format the GPU's math units can process efficiently without wasting cycles waiting for memory.
